description: UIAO federal-whitepaper SVG figure palette and canvas tokens (ADR-093). Single source for diagram colors and conventions; SVGs reference these hex values.

navy.use: primary node fills, box backgrounds, structural elements

teal.use: pipeline arrows, connectors, status-nominal accents, 'good' states

teal_tint.use: light teal fills behind 'AD / native' content

amber.use: HIGH/CRITICAL severity or escalation ONLY — use sparingly

amber_tint.use: light amber fills for emphasis callouts

red_tint.use: light red fills behind loss/cost content

ice.use: light navy tint for cloud/Entra boxes (always paired with a navy border)

white.use: background — always white; no photos, no people, no vendor logos

rules: White background always. No photographs, no human figures, no vendor logos.
Navy for solid/structural ('what AD had'); ice+navy-border for cloud/Entra boxes; red for loss/gap; teal for good/native; amber ONLY for high-severity or escalation.
Every text string is real SVG <text>/<tspan> — never rely on a generative engine. Spell everything correctly; pre-wrap long lines into tspans.
Spell out numbers/dates as words where they would otherwise read oddly is NOT required in SVG (text is literal), but keep labels terse.
Engineering-blueprint style: rectangles, rounded rectangles, directional arrows, node + edge labels. No artistic flourish.
